headline: Zyxel GS1900 patch bypassed, OpenSSH CVE-2026-123158 exploited, SonicWall SSLVPN flaw in CISA KEV; Perry Johnson breach settlement

bullets.text: New: state attorneys general secured up to $10 million and a corrective action plan from the Perry Johnson companies over their 2023 breach. Nothing else new at high severity this run; SITCON holds at 3 (ELEVATED), last 7 days at 0.66x the 90-day average.

Still active, Zyxel GS1900, 4 outlets and top story: Zyxel's fix did not block the in-the-wild exploit (CVE-2026-107441) used to hack nearly 1,000 switches, which allows root command execution. D-Link separately warned of multiple zero-days in DGS-3130 Series switches.

Still active, OpenSSH, 5 outlets: CVE-2026-123158 is exploited in the wild hours after disclosure. Related: OpenSSH's emergency fix for long passwords bypassing SSH auth on Alpine Linux, which also reaches routers.

Still active, SonicWall, 4 outlets: CISA added SonicOS SSLVPN CVE-2026-19868 (use of single-factor authentication) to KEV on 2026-11-06, federal due date 2026-11-20. SecurityWeek also reports SonicWall won't fix flaws in GMS.

Exposed secrets, 3 outlets: hackers are using Artex to scan GitHub repositories for exposed secrets; Microsoft reports threat actors using agentic AI tooling to find and abuse them, and Truffle Security launched a program to revoke nearly 1.5 million live secrets.

Breaches still on the board: Chainalysis says credentials for all customers were exposed and it shut down key services; DigiCert exposed business customer information and identity documents; DreamHost exposed FTP logins and webmail sessions (3 outlets).

actions: Treat Zyxel GS1900 and D-Link DGS-3130 switches as exposed: restrict management access, check for compromise, apply fixes as they ship.
Patch OpenSSH on every internet-facing host now for CVE-2026-123158; restrict SSH exposure and review auth logs for exploitation.
SonicWall SSLVPN users: patch or mitigate CVE-2026-19868 before 2026-11-20, enforce MFA on VPN access, and review VPN logs for unusual logins.
Scan your GitHub repos and their history for committed secrets; revoke and rotate anything found and turn on secret scanning with push protection.
Chainalysis, DigiCert and DreamHost customers: reset passwords, rotate API keys and FTP credentials, and watch for phishing.
WordPress Core CVE-2026-119977 is past its KEV due date: patch now; schedule Ivanti CVE-2026-104935 (due 11-13) and Apple CVE-2024-27834 (due 11-18).
